water.name: Land
water.rule: At least 4 of the hex's 7 sample points (centre + 6) fall on Census state or Natural Earth country outlines, unless the centre is sea and the ETOPO1 mean is at or below sea level, or at least half its ETOPO1 samples are (tidal bays such as the Chesapeake stay water).

water.name: Ocean
water.rule: Sea deeper than 200 m and not next to land.

water.name: Coast
water.rule: Sea next to a land hex, or shallower than 200 m (ETOPO1 mean).

water.name: Lake
water.rule: Water hex (most of its 7 sample points off land) with Natural Earth 1:50m lake points that outnumber sea points, or above sea level.

relief.name: Flat
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation inside the hex under 85 m.

relief.name: Mountains
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation ≥ 260 m, or mean elevation ≥ 2,300 m.

cover.name: None
cover.rule: Water, foreign land, or no NLCD land pixels.

cover.name: Deciduous forest
cover.rule: Forest (41+42+43) is the largest group and deciduous (41) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Conifer forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and evergreen (42) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Mixed forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and mixed (43) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Scrub & desert
cover.rule: Shrub/scrub (52) is the largest group: deserts, chaparral, sagebrush.

cover.name: Grassland
cover.rule: Grassland/herbaceous (71) plus developed open space (21: lawns, parks) is the largest group.

cover.name: Cropland
cover.rule: Cultivated crops (82) is the largest group.

cover.name: Wetland
cover.rule: Woody (90) plus emergent herbaceous (95) wetlands is the largest group.

cover.name: Urban
cover.rule: Developed low/medium/high intensity (22+23+24) is ≥ 30% of the hex's land, whatever else is there.

cover.name: Barren
cover.rule: Barren land (31: rock, sand, playa) is the largest group.

cover.name: Ice & snow
cover.rule: Perennial ice/snow (12) is the largest group.

notes.water: Census 1:20M state outlines and Natural Earth 1:50m country and lake outlines don't meet exactly. A sea hex whose ETOPO1 mean is above sea level (and under half of its samples below it) becomes land when at least 4 of its 6 neighbours are land, or when it touches both US and foreign land; it takes the neighbours' majority owner. Narrow reservoirs that cover less than half a hex are land, and their river is drawn through them. Tidal bays stay water when the hex centre is sea and its ETOPO1 mean is at or below sea level or at least half of its ETOPO1 samples are. A sea hex's elevation is the mean of its ETOPO1 samples below sea level (its water depth).
notes.relief: From ETOPO1 samples (~9 km apart, about 20 per hex) with altitude ≥ -100 m, so bays and sea floor don't count; all samples are used if none qualify. Water hexes are always flat.
notes.cover: From NLCD 2021 (~2 km pixels), sampled on a 2 km lattice inside each US hex (about 400 points). Open water (11) and no-data pixels are ignored; shares are of the remaining land points, rounded to whole percent, and the urban threshold is applied to the rounded developed share. NLCD covers only the lower 48, so foreign hexes (Canada, Mexico, the Caribbean) have cover 0 (none).
